record.paper_title: Distinct Distances: Open Problems and Current Bounds
record.original_question: Let D_line(m,n) be the minimum number of distinct distances between a set of m points on a line and a set of n unrestricted points in R^2. Determine the asymptotic order of D_line(m,n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $m$ and $n$, let $D_{\text{line}}(m,n)$ denote the minimum, over all choices of a set $P_1$ of $m$ points lying on a single line $\ell \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ and a set $P_2$ of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ (with no restriction on $P_2$), of the number of distinct values in the multiset
$$\{\,\|p-q\|_2 : p \in P_1,\ q \in P_2\,\},$$
where $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Euclidean norm. Determine the asymptotic order of $D_{\text{line}}(m,n)$ as $m,n \to \infty$; that is, find matching (up to constants and logarithmic factors) lower and upper bounds for $D_{\text{line}}(m,n)$ in terms of $m$ and $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears open. Bruner and Sharir (Discrete Mathematics, 2018) obtained a lower bound of Ω(min{m^{2/3}n^{2/3}, m^{4/11}n^{10/11}log^{-2/11}m, m^2, n^2}) only under the additional restriction that every line parallel or orthogonal to ℓ contains O(1) points of the arbitrary set. Without such restrictions, no matching bounds for D_line(m,n) appear in the literature; subsequent work (e.g., bipartite distinct distances papers from 2019 onward) treats related but distinct configurations.

status_evidence.title: Distinct distances between a collinear set and an arbitrary set of points
status_evidence.snippet: Bruner and Sharir prove Ω(min{n^{2/3}m^{2/3}, n^{10/11}m^{4/11} log^{2/11} m, n^2, m^2}) lower bound under restriction that no hyperplane orthogonal to ℓ and no hypercylinder with axis ℓ contains more than O(1) points of P_2.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial lower bounds are known, under additional restrictions on the arbitrary point set.

status_evidence.title: On Bipartite Distinct Distances in the Plane
status_evidence.snippet: Studies bipartite distinct distances between point sets on lines/curves but does not resolve D_line(m,n) for one set on a line and one unrestricted set.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent bipartite distinct distances work does not settle the asymptotic order of D_line(m,n).
